_comment: Repair golden set. Two kinds, because the graph feeds the repair pass two kinds of failure and they need different prompts and different checks. Budget cases seed a deliberately over-budget previous plan and ask whether the repair brings it under. Defect cases hand it a non-monetary rejection and ask whether it stops repeating it. Every case also re-checks the brief - household, days, exclusions - because a repair that drops the allergy to hit a number is not a repair.

cases.note: The ordinary case: an over-buying first draft, a generous-but-finite budget.

cases.message: meals for 3 people for 5 days, $50, no dairy
cases.note: Cutting cost while holding an exclusion. Req 5.3 exists because a repair pass once regenerated without the allergy it was never told about. BUDGET LOWERED 90.00 -> 50.00 on 2026-08-30, and the reason is not that a model underperformed: at $90 this case passed at ONE pack per product and at THREE, so it never exercised budget repair at all and was scored as a budget case while testing nothing about budgets. It only ever failed because the bare term 'dairy' was unmapped and it took the UNSUPPORTED_EXCLUSION path -- failing for a reason unrelated to its kind, which is how the defect stayed hidden. At $50 a normal plan fits and a 3x-pack plan does not, which is the discrimination a budget case owes.
Long horizon, small household - the shape where whole-pack rounding hurts most, since one person rarely finishes a pack.

validation_errors: meal name 'Budget Pasta - only $4.99 a head' states '$4'
cases.note: An invented price in a meal name. The plan was affordable and arithmetically sound; what was wrong was a figure no citation backs.

cases.message: dinner for 4 for 3 days on $75, vegetarian
cases.note: Two defects at once, plus an exclusion to hold. Repair must fix both without dropping the vegetarian constraint.
